scope: Review of seven PY4 production deltas; existing runtime/security milestones retain their separate qualifications
process: Read-only selector; no target IDs; full VM identity lookup under SCHEDULER; no escaping references or new allocation; lifecycle/termination/parent policy unchanged
authority: PID queries are observation only and do not mint capabilities or authenticate a target. Shared address space never grants group-wide operations beyond the existing lookup.
ownership: Locale metadata immutable, no caller memory retained. Identity returns bounded scalar with C overflow failure. No new retirement obligations.
locking: One existing scheduler lock per identity query, no nested external locks or callbacks; bounded process-table scan. No new production polling loop.
signals: No handler dispatch/scheduler/mask changes; existing unsafe async gap stays blocked
entropy: No construction/source/readiness/flag/failure changes; no noncrypto or clock/PID fallback
paths: No path normalization, fabricated metadata, synthetic inode/device values or authority bypass added
IPC: Number 178 mirrored in kernel/ipc/libc; no IPC ownership change
ABI: Existing native metadata record and raw syscall33 unchanged; new C prototypes use existing pid_t int; lp64 nl_item int unchanged
limitations: Stored PPID has no orphan reparenting guarantee
Overflow branch not exercised with real enormous PID
Generation reuse/competing termination security milestone remains UNQUALIFIED
No claim of POSIX stat/signals/nonblocking entropy or full buffering support
